text:
eli park: starting onboarding for customer Zeppelin's LoRA v1. different smoke: focusing on currency formatting + token merges under int4/int3 quant paths. kicking off quickpack now.

eli park: command: `./run_quickpack --base pegasus-13b --lora zeppelin_v1.safetensors --quant int4 --checks invoice_format,token_stability --out runs/zepp_qp1`

nina rao: ping on adding the 'leading_hash' test set (contains cases like '#INV000', '#INV 000', '# INV-123'). those were flaky before.

matt c: note from last customer call: they used a custom byte-pair for '#INV' and also registered 'CUR:' as a single token. token merge needs to preserve both.

sylvia (eval-bot): run queued id=qp-2024-11-13-01-1111, node p-qe-gpu-07. posting live progress to runs/zepp_qp1/status.log

eli park: initial results: 4/8 checks failed. main two: (1) invoice token splitting (we output '#', 'INV' tokens), (2) decimal rounding for large amounts (e.g., expected '1,234.50' got '1234.5'). snippet from output: `got: "INV-045" expected: "#INV-045"`

nina rao: decimal issue could be coming from fp->int quant rounding in the tokenizer post-processing. did quantizer run with 'round-half-to-even' policy?

matt c: quant config used default `quant_cfg.json` which sets rounding=trunc. that might explain consistent drop of trailing zero. try `rounding=bankers` to preserve .50.

eli park: checking token merge logs: `merge_tokens.log` shows warnings: `OVERRIDE: '#INV' collides with existing sequence '#' + 'INV' at ids [50123, 32012] -> creating alias`.

nina rao: that aliasing will break generation because customer finetune expects atomic token. can we force a stable id remap before quant prune?

matt c: propose patchflow: (a) create pre-merge vocab mapping file locking '#INV' and 'CUR:' ids to the customer's original ids; (b) run `merge_lora.py --vocab-lock zep_vocab_lock.json`; (c) quantize with `--preserve-ids` and `--rounding bankers`.

sylvia (eval-bot): advisory: quant pipeline currently prunes unused tokens under aggressive prune_mode=aggressive. recommend prune_mode=conservative for customer models that rely on special tokens.

eli park: applying patch now. zep_vocab_lock.json contains: `{"#INV":"50123","CUR:":"60201"}`. re-running with conservative prune and bankers rounding.

ops-bot: infra note - job 54901 started on p-qe-gpu-12, ETA ~3m.

sylvia (eval-bot): re-run complete qp-2024-11-13-01-1712. results: 7/8 pass. invoice tokens preserved, decimal formatting fixed. regression: one behavioral drift on paraphrase consistency (ROUGE-L down 1.1 pts on long-descriptions). full report: s3://redwood-evals/zepp/onboard/qpack-1748701712/report.html

nina rao: paraphrase drift likely from small LoRA weight influence under int4 quant. may need a floating-point warm path (int8 for KV cache) or a short canary on dedicated infra.

matt c: agree. we can enable mixed-precision KV cache (int8) for canary and see if paraphrase quality recovers. also add a small unit test: ensure any token in customer_protected_tokens.txt remains single-token after merge. I'll open PR for both the test and the `quant_cfg` change.

eli park: I'll notify AE and mark this quickpack green for go/no-go, but schedule dedicated perf+quality canary with mixed-KV in prod-sim next week. cc @nina rao. :white_check_mark:

sylvia (eval-bot): note: latency impact estimate for mixed-KV int8 on p-dedicated-gpu is +6-9% p95, cost +8%.

ops-bot: scheduled canary job id=canary-1748780000 for 2024-11-20 14:00 UTC on group p-dedicated-gpu-c1.

nina rao: thanks team. small follow-up: add 'token-stability' check to pre-merge CI and set default prune_mode=conservative for any customer LoRA merges.

matt c: PR incoming (link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/merge-tool/pull/289) with tests + quant defaults.

eli park: closing thread, saving artifacts and annotating customer ticket with details and S3 artifacts.
